prompt:
An industrial electric hoist on a construction site lifts a steel beam of mass 850 kg vertically upwards at a steady speed of 0.40 m s^-1 through a height of 24 m. The electric motor is supplied with a constant electrical power of 5.2 kW. (Take g = 9.81 m s^-2).
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Schematic diagram showing an electric hoist motor winding a steel cable to lift a heavy steel beam of mass 850 kg vertically at constant speed v = 0.40 m s^-1 through height h = 24 m. An oil cooling reservoir absorbs heat dissipated by the motor windings.]
(a) Calculate the tension force in the lifting cable during the lift. [1]
(b) Calculate the useful mechanical power output developed by the hoist. [2]
(c) Calculate the efficiency of the hoist system. [1]
(d) The motor is cooled by oil circulating through a heat exchanger.
(i) Calculate the rate at which thermal energy is dissipated by the motor during the lift. [1]
(ii) Calculate the total thermal energy transferred to the cooling oil during the complete 24 m lift. [1]

parts.description: Calculate tension force from weight at constant speed
Calculate useful power output from force and speed
Calculate rate of thermal energy dissipation
Calculate total thermal energy dissipated during complete lift

part_enrichment.guidance: Award A1 for T = mg = 850 * 9.81 = 8340 N (accept 8300 N).
part_enrichment.common_pitfalls: Attempting complex dynamics when motion is at constant speed (acceleration is zero).

part_enrichment.guidance: Award M1 for P = Tv = 8338.5 * 0.40, A1 for 3340 W (or 3300 W / 3.34 kW).
part_enrichment.common_pitfalls: Multiplying by height instead of velocity, confusing work with power.
Inverting the ratio or omitting the percentage sign when writing 64.

part_enrichment.guidance: Award A1 for P_waste = 5200 - 3335 = 1865 W approx 1900 W (or 1.86 kW).
part_enrichment.common_pitfalls: Subtracting useful work instead of useful power from input power.

part_enrichment.guidance: Award A1 for time = 24 / 0.40 = 60 s, then E = 1865 * 60 = 1.1 * 10^5 J (or 112 kJ).
part_enrichment.common_pitfalls: Forgetting to calculate the total lift time or using 24 s.

hints: In (a), at steady speed the upward cable tension equals the weight of the beam.
In (b), calculate useful mechanical power using P = Fv.
In (c), efficiency is useful power output divided by electrical power input.
In (d)(i), wasted power is the difference between input power and useful power.
In (d)(ii), find the time taken for the lift (t = h / v) and multiply by the wasted power.
solution:
(a) Because the beam rises at constant speed, acceleration is zero: T = mg = 850 kg * 9.81 m s^-2 = 8338.5 N approx 8340 N (8.34 kN).
(b) Useful power output P_useful = Tv = 8338.5 N * 0.40 m s^-1 = 3335.4 W approx 3340 W (3.34 kW).
(c) Efficiency eta = P_useful / P_in = 3335.4 W / 5200 W = 0.6414 = 64% (or 0.64).
(d)(i) Rate of thermal energy dissipation P_waste = P_in - P_useful = 5200 W - 3335.4 W = 1864.6 W approx 1900 W (1.86 kW).
(d)(ii) Time for lift t = h / v = 24 m / 0.40 m s^-1 = 60 s. Total heat transferred to oil = P_waste * t = 1864.6 W * 60 s = 111 876 J approx 1.1 * 10^5 J (112 kJ).
teacher_walkthrough: Structured multipart question testing mechanics, power, efficiency, and thermal energy dissipation.
Verify that students distinguish between power (watts) in part (d)(i) and energy (joules) in part (d)(ii).
